evals.prompt:
Brainstorm 4 alternative one-sentence mnemonic story candidates for the word "creak."

Word: creak
Pronunciation: KREEK /krik/
Definition: A long, harsh squeaking or groaning sound, like the one an old wooden door, floorboard, or hinge makes when it moves.
Sound axis: "creak" is a perfect homophone of "creek" — they sound identical.
Meaning axis (already drafted): Picture an old wooden bridge over a creek, groaning with a loud creak every time someone crosses — the tavern door makes that same sound.
evals.expected_output: 4 new one-sentence story candidates, each depicting a single coherent physical scene (indoor OR outdoor, not both) where a creek and the creaking object could plausibly coexist. Ground truth failure mode: an earlier run produced 'Stepping past the creek, the attic floorboard creaks beneath my feet' — an attic is indoors under a roof and cannot be adjacent to an outdoor creek, so the scene doesn't hang together even though each half is individually vivid.
assertions: No candidate combines an indoor-only setting (attic, basement, hallway) with an outdoor creek in the same sentence

Every candidate's setting/objects could physically coexist in one real-world place at the same time (e.g. a cabin door BY a creek, a dock ON a creek, a rowboat ON a creek — not a creek stitched onto an unrelated indoor room)
All candidates still use a perfect creak/creek homophone anchor
Each candidate is one sentence, ≤15 words
Candidates show genuine variety in scene/object (not near-duplicates of each other or of the saved bridge/tavern-door story)

evals.prompt:
Brainstorm one-sentence mnemonic story candidates for the word "adjacent."

Word: adjacent
Pronunciation: uh-JAY-sunt /əˈdʒeɪsənt/
Definition: Adjacent means right next to something else, sharing a border or edge — like two adjacent rooms sharing a wall.
Sound axis: "adjacent" hides the name "Jason" almost whole — a-JASON-t.
Meaning axis (already drafted): picture Jason living in the house right next door — that's adjacent: immediately next to, sharing a border.
evals.expected_output: Story candidates that anchor on "Jason" and depict a single physically consistent model of adjacency — either a shared border/wall (no direct contact between the objects on either side) or direct touching (no wall/separator mentioned) — not both at once. Ground truth failure mode: a candidate combined 'Jason's dorm bed touches mine, our rooms share one thin wall' — a wall between two rooms means the beds on either side of it cannot also touch each other, so the two clauses contradict rather than reinforce one scene.
assertions: No candidate states or implies a wall/partition/border separates two objects AND that the same two objects are in direct physical contact
Each candidate commits to one physical model of adjacency (contact-through-a-shared-boundary, or direct-touching-with-no-boundary-mentioned) and stays consistent within the sentence
All candidates anchor "Jason" against the uh-JAY-sunt / əˈdʒeɪsənt pronunciation
Each candidate is one sentence, ≤15 words
Candidates show genuine variety in scene/object, not near-duplicates of each other
